docs.title: About
docs.text:
This is a complete documentation for creating entities in RLD+ with the help of the Entity module/class made by Avery.

The module is still work in progress and there will be more features to come.

docs.title: Constructing
docs.text:
Creating an entity is as simple as follows:

EntityData.lua
-- Paste this code inside a ModuleScript and put it inside your entity model.
local EntityModel = script.Parent
local EntityData = {
    Type = "Generic"; -- (1)

    Speed = 25; -- (2)
    SpawnLocation = 0; -- (3)

    Direction = "Forward"; -- (4)
}

return EntityData
  1. This will set the entity type to a generic entity.
  2. This will make the entity move at the speed of 25 studs per second.
  3. This will make the entity spawn at the starting room (room 0)
  4. This will make the entity move forward (from the starting room to the last room)

The framework will automatically construct an entity with an existing model that has a speed of 25 studs/second, spawns at the first room and goes forward to the last room.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
To add your own functionality to the entity, you can add a callback function directly inside your settings table to make the entity run code.

EntityData.lua
local EntityData = {
    ...
    OnSpawn = function(Entity) -- (1)
        print("The entity has spawned!")
        -- your code goes here lulz
    end,
    OnFinished = function(Entity) -- (2)
        Print("The entity has finished!")
        -- code goes here. braah
    end,
}

return EntityData
  1. This will bind a function to the OnSpawn callback which will be called when the entity is about to spawn.
  2. This will bind a function to the OnFinished callback which will be called when the entity is about to finish it's sequence.

The Entity parameter is the entity class itself. Which contain important properties, methods and events like the entity's current State, core methods like Entity:CanSeeTarget()

docs.title: AddToJanitor
docs.text:
Passes the given object to the entity's janitor to be destroyed/disconnected on entity destruction. If a function is passed, it will be called when the entity is destroyed. 

Entity:AddToJanitor(object: T,methodName?: boolean|string,index?) : T
Parameters

object : Variant The object you want to clean up. methodName? : boolean | string The name of the method that will be used to clean up. If not passed, it will first check if the object's type exists in TypeDefaults, and if that doesn't exist, it assumes Destroy. index? : unknown The index that can be used to clean up the object manually.

Returns

Variant The object that was passed as the first argument.

The entity's type that the entity will be using.

docs.title: SpawnLocation
docs.text:
The entity's spawn location, which is a room number. 

EntityData.SpawnLocation : number

= 1

Tip

To make the entity spawn at the last room, set the value to game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedVariables._NUMBER.Value.Value

Warning

We currently don't have a better implementation for spawning entities at the current room. This may be subject to change in the future or not.

docs.title: SpawnOffset
docs.text:
Determines how the entity is offset from it's SpawnLocation, relative to the global axes. 

EntityData.SpawnOffset : Vector3
= Vector3.zero

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
The entity's movement speed. Which can be set to a number or a SpeedData dictionary for more variety. 

EntityData.Speed : number | SpeedData
= 0

docs.title: AltPath
docs.text:
Determines whether or not the entity will follow an alternative path. 

EntityData.AltPath : boolean
= false

When this setting is set to true, the entity, instead of following the main path, will look for an alternative path to follow for each room it enters. When there are no alternative paths to find, it will follow the main path instead as a failsafe.

docs.title: Sequence
docs.text:
Determines which room should the entity go to. 

EntityData.Sequence : number
= 0

Info

Setting the value to any number higher than the last room will make the entity go to the last room dynamically.

docs.title: Direction
docs.text:
Determines the entity's move direction. 

EntityData.Direction : Enum.EntityDirection
= "Forward"

When set to "Forward", the entity will move from the starting room (last room if set to "Backwards") to the room number set in [Sequence].

docs.title: Rebounds
docs.text:
How many times will the entity rebound for. 

EntityData.Rebounds : number
= 0

docs.title: CanDestroyObstructions
docs.text:
Enables a feature where if the entity reaches the last room (assuming the entity has finished it's moving sequence), the entity will destroy the next room door and force generate a room. 

EntityData.CanDestroyObstructions : boolean
= false

docs.title: Entity Type
docs.text:
Used by the entity class to identify what entity type it is.

Name Description Generic The entity is a generic entity. Chaser The entity is a chasing entity. Checker The entity is a locker checking entity. Summoner The entity is an entity that summons other entities.

docs.title: Entity Direction
docs.text:
Used by the entity to determine which direction the entity is moving towards.

Name Description Forward The entity is moving forwards. Backward The entity is moving backwards.

docs.title: Entity State
docs.text:
Used by the entity to determine which state the entity is in.

Name Description Unloaded The entity is unloaded. Loaded The entity has successfully loaded. Idle The entity is idling. Moving The entity is moving. Deactivated The entity is is deactivated. Not to be confused with Entity.isActive, the entity will enter this state when the entity has ended it's event sequence

docs.title: Hiding Spots
docs.text:
Used by the framework to determine what hiding spot the player is currently in.

Name Description Table The hiding spot is a generic table. Locker The hiding spot is a generic locker. BlueLocker The hiding spot is a BLUE locker.

docs.title: Spawning
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    SpawnLocation = 0;
    SpawnOffset = Vector3.new(0,25,0);
}
This will make the entity spawn at the starting room (a.k.a Room 0) and offsets it's spawn location 25 studs on the Y axis.

Tip

To make the entity spawn at the last room, set the SpawnLocation to game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedVariables._NUMBER.Value.Value

Warning

We currently don't have a better implementation for spawning entities at the current room. This may be subject to change in the future or not.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Speed = 50;
    Direction = "Forward";
    Rebounds = 1;
}
This will make the entity move forward (from the starting room to the last room) at 50 studs per second and rebounds once.

docs.title: Blacklisting hiding spots
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    ProhibitedSpots = {}
}
The ProhibitedSpots setting will make it so that any players that are hiding in a spot that has been added to the ProhibitedSpots array are considered not hiding and the entity will attempt to damage/chase the player depending on the entity's type.

To add a hiding spot to be excluded from valid hiding spots, do: 

EntityData = {
    ProhibitedSpots = {"Table","your_hiding_spot_id"} -- Add more excluded hiding spots here
}
The list of all hiding spots are in the enums hiding spot category.

docs.title: Damaging
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    DamagePerRate = 20;
    DamageDelay = 0.5; -- in seconds
    HitboxRadius = 14;
    Raycasting = true;
}
This will make the entity damage players by taking 20 points of their health every 0.5 seconds and has a radius of 14 studs.

The Raycasting setting will make it so that entities can only damage players if the entity is in line of sight of the player. However, if the player is hiding, the entity will not damage them unless they're hiding in one of the ProhibitedSpots

docs.title: Jumpscaring
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Jumpscare = "entity_name"
}
This will jumpscare the player with the specified Jumpscare setting. By default, the jumpscare will trigger when the player dies.

docs.title: Screen Shake
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Screenshake = {
        ['Range'] = 10,
        ['Strength'] = 0,
        ['Roughness'] = 15,
        ['FadeIn'] = 0.25,
        ['FadeOut'] = .65,
        ['V3_PosInfluence'] = Vector3.zero,
        ['V3_RotInfluence'] = Vector3.new(1,1,2)
    }
}

Entities use CameraShaker module for visualizing camera shake. Check out CameraShaker's devforum post to learn more about how to use it.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text: Entities are designed to be fully customizable. Aside from basic settings, you can code your own entity to do whatever you want it to do.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Entities have events that you can listen for and respond to. They fires in response to specific actions or changes.

For example, an entity has rebounded: 

Entity.OnRebound:Connect(function(rebounds: number, direction: string)
    print("The entity has rebounded",rebounds,"times and is heading",direction)
end)
Or, an entity has finished it's sequence and about to be unloaded: 
Entity.OnEnded:Connect(function()
    print("The entity has completed")
end)
Or, an entity damages a player: 
Entity.OnHit:Connect(function(player: Player)
    print("The entity dealt damage to",player)
end)

docs.title: Entity Types
docs.text:
EntityData = {
    Type = "Generic" -- this is a required setting, put your entity type in here
}
Aside from general entities, there are other variety of entity types like Hiding Spot Checkers, Summoners and Chasers. Each type has their own properties but are mostly inherited by the Generic type.

Warning

The Type setting is required and must be included in every EntityData setting module.

Check the API Reference for more info on different Entity types.

docs.title: SpeedData
docs.text: An alternative dictionary containing the entity's speed data. Allows for more speed customization

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
The speed of the entity in studs per second. 

SpeedData.Speed : number

docs.title: Acceleration
docs.text:
How fast the entity will accelerate. 

SpeedData.Acceleration : number
The entity will have it's base speed incremented by Acceleration every second.

If acceleration is a negative value, the entity will decelerate instead.

docs.title: MinSpeed
docs.text:
The minimum speed the entity can decelerate. 

SpeedData.MinSpeed : number

docs.title: MaxSpeed
docs.text:
The maximum speed the entity can accelerate. 

SpeedData.MaxSpeed : number

docs.title: PingPong
docs.text:
Determines whether the entity's speed will go back and forth between MinSpeed and MaxSpeed or stand still. 

SpeedData.PingPong : boolean
When set to true, the entity's speed (if acceleration is not 0) will accelerate to MaxSpeed and then decelerates to MinSpeed. This process will repeat until the entity is inactive.
